identity.title: Plant Operator: commissioning a condensing steam cycle

outcomes.statement: Compute cycle thermal efficiency, net specific work, turbine-exit quality and required mass flow for a Rankine cycle with non-ideal turbomachinery.
Predict and explain the effect of boiler pressure, superheat temperature and condenser pressure on efficiency and on turbine-exit quality.
Identify operating points that violate the turbine-exit moisture limit and select an admissible design point.

misconceptions.description: Believing that raising condenser pressure improves output.
Believing higher boiler pressure always improves efficiency, ignoring the moisture constraint.
Conflating cycle thermal efficiency with turbine isentropic efficiency.
Neglecting pump work as automatically negligible without checking its magnitude.
Applying the isentropic efficiency to the enthalpy rather than to the isentropic enthalpy drop.

displays: Live T-s diagram with the four state points
State-point table (p, T, h, s, x)
Turbine-exit quality with shaded inadmissible region below x_min
Required mass flow for the target net power

scaffold_ladder.support: The T-s diagram is annotated with state-point labels and the moisture limit is shaded from the first interaction.
After four evaluations with no change to condenser pressure, a prompt invites the learner to sweep it and observe the effect on both efficiency and exit quality.
After eight evaluations with no admissible point found, the simulator offers a worked partial derivation of x4 for the learner's current point.
On request, a fully worked example at a different, non-graded operating point.

constraints.expression: exists an operating point satisfying all limits
constraints.rationale: Semantic invariance: every instance must be solvable, or difficulty is not constant across students.
The binding constraint must be consequential, otherwise the instance does not assess LO3.
Keeps the required mass flow within the range of a physically plausible unit.
Physical bounds; violation indicates a defect in the generated model, not a hard instance.

observables.description: Number of distinct operating points evaluated before submission.
Whether the learner entered and then left the inadmissible-moisture region (evidence of constraint discovery).
Whether the pressure sweep was systematic (monotonic, one variable at a time) or unstructured.
Time from first interaction to first admissible operating point.
Final recorded design point (all control values).

gradebook.aggregation: Natural weighting; quiz 70%, Workshop submission + assessment 30%
completion_conditions: H5P activity viewed and a design point recorded
restrict_access: Quiz available only after the H5P activity reaches completion
Workshop opens after the quiz closes

immediate.message: Efficiency fell. Raising condenser pressure raises the temperature at which you reject heat, which reduces the available work.

immediate.trigger: operating point enters the shaded region
immediate.message: Exit quality is now below your unit's limit. This point is inadmissible regardless of its efficiency; blade erosion is the reason the limit exists.
Note what happened to exit quality as turbine efficiency rose. Efficiency and admissibility are pulling in opposite directions here.

per_try: Start from the four state points. State 1 is saturated liquid at the condenser pressure; state 3 is the turbine inlet.
Find the isentropic exit state first: s4s = s3, so x4s = (s3 - sf)/sfg. Apply the isentropic efficiency to the enthalpy drop, not to the enthalpy.
If your efficiency is high but your exit quality is below x_min, the design point is inadmissible for your unit.
feedback.post_hoc: Worked method for the learner's own instance, with the computed exit quality compared against the learner's x_min, delivered as question general feedback.

accessibility.equivalent_task_pathway: A tabulated state-point dataset covering the learner's instance, supplied as an accessible HTML table, with the same Formulas question and the same Workshop task. Grades are identical in weight and construct.

limiting_cases.expected: Reduces to the ideal Rankine cycle; efficiency matches the textbook ideal value for 8 MPa/480 C/10 kPa.
Net work becomes negative once pump work exceeds turbine work; the solver must report infeasibility rather than a negative efficiency.
Net work and efficiency tend to zero.
